subject: Tenant On-Prem Handshake — routing matrix, runbook, and canary cutover agenda
summary: Coordination thread with StellarBank infra to validate control-plane/data-plane routing matrix, exchange reference diagrams, and lock a canary cutover window. Action items: validate NAT/egress path, confirm KMS boundary, and sign off on runbook handoff.

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@stellarbank.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: infra@stellarbank.com
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood private deploy — request to validate routing matrix and runbook

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our infra team has sketched an initial routing matrix and a first-pass runbook for an on-prem tenant attachment (attached). Before we lock a cutover window we need Redwood to:

- Confirm control plane <-> data plane egress paths (especially for telemetry and KV sync).
- Validate NAT and egress requirements from tenant VPCs to Redwood control endpoints.
- Confirm KMS/HSM boundary for model key material and whether we need an additional LB in front of the control plane.

Would it be possible to do a focused review tomorrow morning (PST)? We can provide diagrams and network ACLs.

Attachments: SB-Staged-Network-Matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Maria
Lead Platform Engineer, StellarBank

Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — request to validate routing matrix and runbook

Maria — thanks, got the matrix. Looping in Aditya (networking) and Kimberly (ops/runbook) for technical validation.

Proposed agenda for a 45-minute review:
1) Quick alignment (5m): scope + success criteria for canary tenant (latency SLO and telemetry retention).
2) Control/data routing (15m): examine edge relays, NAT, and port allowlists. Clarify which telemetry endpoints need outbound reachability vs. proxied relay.
3) Key management (10m): where model keys live, required egress for HSM/KMS calls, and customer-managed key options.
4) Runbook & cutover checklist (10m): who executes steps, rollback triggers, and observability asserts.
5) Action items & schedule (5m).

Please confirm if 08:30-09:15 PST tomorrow works or suggest a slot. Also attach the diagrams you want us to review in the meeting (network and control-plane sequence diagram).

Sofia
Head of Private Deploys, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com

Folks — I reviewed SB-Staged-Network-Matrix.xlsx and sketched a concise reference artifact (attached) that maps control-plane endpoints, data-plane egress requirements, and preferred proxy/MTLS hops. Key notes:

- Control plane (Redwood CP) requires outbound MTLS to our control endpoint pool: cp1.redwood-inference.internal:443 and cp2.redwood-inference.internal:443. Our recommended pattern is: tenant VMs -> tenant edge relay (in-customer) -> outbound NAT gateway -> egress proxy (customer-provided or Redwood-managed) -> Redwood CP.
- Telemetry: streaming metrics (OTLP) should be proxied via the egress proxy to avoid direct CP exposure. If Stellar wants to host a relay in their DMZ, we recommend a 2-way MTLS channel with mutual auth and pinning to our intermediate cert.
- KV sync (KV cache consistency): allows only TCP 443 outbound to a whitelist of IPs; we provide a static set for canary.
- KMS/HSM: If Stellar uses a customer-managed HSM that must not be reachable from outside their network, Redwood can call a customer-side HSM via a secure proxy. If they insist on external KMS calls, we require specific firewall rules (listed in the matrix).

I've attached: redwood-control-data-reference.xlsx (routing matrix) and redwood-runbook-v2.pdf (first-pass). Please pull the diagram in the drive link and confirm the NAT behavior for their staging subnet.

Attachments: redwood-control-data-reference.xlsx, redwood-runbook-v2.pdf

Aditya
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — request to validate routing matrix and runbook

Thanks — saw Aditya's attachments. A few operational clarifications before the review:

- Rollback: define the exact traffic cut (route withdraw vs. DNS flip). For canary we prefer a route-based traffic steering so rollback is immediate. Need Stellar to confirm their BGP or internal route configuration capability.
- Observability asserts: must include token-level generation rate, CPU/GPU backpressure alarms, and KV-sync lag > 500ms as a critical rollback trigger.
- Cutover runner: propose Stellar runs steps 1-3 (edge relay config, NAT mapping, ACL apply), Redwood runs model pin/update and live checks.

I've converted our runbook notes to a checklist (canary-plan-checklist.md) and attached. Also flagged a small doc gap around cert rotation for edge relays — Aditya, can you confirm pinning requirements?

Attachments: canary-plan-checklist.md

Kimberly
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sofia / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. 08:30-09:15 PST tomorrow works for us (we'll bring network ACLs and the DMZ topology diagram). A couple quick confirmations before the call:

- We will support a route-based canary (BGP communities) and can perform the traffic steering you recommend.
- We'll host an OTLP relay in our DMZ; please share the intermediate cert pining instructions and the static IPs for the canary whitelist.
- KMS: Stellar will host the HSM in an air-gapped vault; we'll provide a secure proxy endpoint during the canary window.

I'll upload the DMZ diagram to the Drive link and invite infra to the meeting. See you tomorrow.

Maria
Lead Platform Engineer, StellarBank
